page: Microsoft Azure E16d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It includes a bundled 614 GB local SSD for high-speed temporary storage, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate solid capabilities across memory-intensive and computational workloads. The server achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1899.39 and a multi-core score of 15536.33. Memory bandwidth is measured at 834.28 GB/sec for small cached blocks, and 96.81 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, with a write speed of 56.93 GB/sec. In application-level tests, the server handles 14.9 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 21.56 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning, it processes 1030.31 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M parameter model, dropping to 34.86 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

Given its high memory density and dedicated CPU allocation, the E16d_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require substantial memory footprints without the overhead of a GPU. The inclusion of a 614 GB local SSD provides a cost-effective alternative to provisioning external storage for temporary files and caching. This hardware profile is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
